_meta.why_v2: Ground-up rebuild (2026-09-11), installed from an owner-supplied rewrite. The v1 five-mode design (spiral/unfreeze/recover/reflect/patterns) replaced with one job: separate what happened from what the visitor's mind added, name what's genuinely unknown, offer at most one grounded next move.
_meta.why_v2_1_and_v2_2: Two live-verification correction passes on the v2 fact-vs-story design: (1) a third-person voice leak from CONTRACT's own heavy use of the word 'visitor' — fixed with a VOICE section; (2) what_is_unknown re-elaborating uncertainty with invented alternative scenarios instead of restoring the one the visitor already named, no status badges rendered for the PREDICTION/INTERPRETATION/CONCLUSION classification, next_move language promising resolution ('that question can only answer itself after contact'), and the spiral-added thought field paraphrasing instead of preserving the visitor's own words.
_meta.why_v3:
Full replacement of the v2 fact-vs-story design (installed from a second owner-supplied rewrite, 2026-09-12). The v2 design stopped after telling the visitor which thoughts were not established — epistemically clean but often not useful enough. v3 adds the actual product job: judge whether there is a real, actionable problem at all (solvability: YES/PARTLY/NOT_YET/NO), then give exactly ONE exit matched to that judgment (ACT/CAPTURE/WAIT/DISENGAGE) plus a reusable first-person stopping rule. Also added: 'Get me out of my head', a client-side, no-API attention-shift micro-flow (4 steps: look away, describe 3 details, notice a sound, choose what's next) — available both before submitting and after results, for when the visitor needs a moment before or after working through the loop. v2's PREDICTION/INTERPRETATION/CONCLUSION enum and next_move field are gone entirely, replaced by loop_summary/what_is_real/what_is_unknown/solvability/exit/stopping_rule.

Carried forward every lesson from the v2 correction passes into v3's CONTRACT from the start: an explicit VOICE section, a WHAT'S UNKNOWN-equivalent 'UNKNOWN' section capped at 2 (code-enforced in validateResult, not just prompt-hoped) with a wrong/right example against inventing alternative scenarios, and a 'PRESERVE THEIR WORDS' rule for loop_summary. Even so, live verification caught ONE new recurrence of the resolution-promising pattern in a different shape: exit.why said 'It ends the delay, which is the only part of this you can actually change' — narrowly true (the delay does end) but the 'only X' framing implies the exit addresses more of the situation than it does, including what's still unknown. Fixed by extending NEVER PROMISE RESOLUTION to explicitly ban 'the only concrete thing'/'the only part you can change' framing, with this exact sentence as the new wrong example. Verified clean across 3 repeated runs after the fix.
_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run cases (npm run check:golden spiral-stopper). Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200, no truncation, SENSITIVE mental-health domain. GUARDS: validateResult() in backend/routes/spiral-stopper.js keys on top-level `safety_redirect` (boolean); caps what_is_real<=3, what_is_unknown<=2; pins solvability.status to YES/PARTLY/NOT_YET/NO (falls back to NO with a conservative headline) and exit.kind to ACT/CAPTURE/WAIT/DISENGAGE (falls back to DISENGAGE with a generic 'stop and redirect attention' action) rather than reaching the visitor malformed. A true safety_redirect forces every other field to its empty/null shape. DO NOT reverse: the two enum whitelists, the array caps, the safety_redirect field-zeroing, or the NEVER PROMISE RESOLUTION discipline (grep new captures for 'only concrete thing'/'only part'/'you'll know' in exit.why or exit.done_when).

input.thoughts: I have not replied to my friends text in four days and I am convinced she thinks I do not care about her and that I have damaged the friendship.
input.actual_event: I have not replied to my friends text in four days.

output.loop_summary: You have not replied to your friend's text in four days and are convinced she thinks you do not care and that the friendship is damaged.
what_is_real: You have not replied to your friend's text in four days.
You have not yet sent a reply.
what_is_unknown: You do not know how your friend has interpreted the delay.

solvability.headline: There is one thing you can do right now.
solvability.explanation: The reply has not been sent, and sending it is something you can do now. What your friend thinks, or how she has interpreted the delay, is not established and is not something you can settle in advance.

exit.action: Reply to her text now. You do not need to explain the four days at length — a normal, direct reply is enough to resume the conversation.
exit.why: Replying gives you something concrete to do instead of trying to pre-solve what her interpretation is.

output.stopping_rule: I can reply; I cannot settle what she thinks before I do.

input.thoughts: I am waiting on biopsy results and my mind keeps jumping straight to the worst case. I have basically already written the whole story in my head.
input.actual_event: I am waiting for biopsy results. I do not have the results yet.

output.loop_summary: Your mind keeps jumping straight to the worst case and you have already written the whole story in your head — before the results exist.
what_is_real: You are waiting for biopsy results.
The results have not arrived yet.

solvability.headline: There is nothing new to solve yet.
solvability.explanation: The only thing that changes this situation is the results arriving. Until then, the story your mind is running is being written without the information it needs.

exit.action: Stop here and let the results be the next chapter. The information that makes this solvable is the result itself — not anything you can think your way to before it arrives.
exit.why: Another run-through of the worst-case story does not add any evidence you do not already have.

output.stopping_rule: I do not have the results yet — there is no story to solve, only one to wait for.

input.thoughts: I said something awkward at a work happy hour and I keep replaying the exact words. I am sure everyone thinks I am weird now.
input.actual_event: I said something at the work happy hour that I now feel awkward about.

output.loop_summary: You said something awkward at a work happy hour and keep replaying the exact words, certain everyone now thinks you are weird.
what_is_real: You said something at the happy hour that you now feel awkward about.
You have been replaying the moment repeatedly since it happened.
what_is_unknown: You do not know how, or whether, anyone else registered what you said.

solvability.headline: There is nothing established here that needs action.
solvability.explanation: No concrete problem has emerged — no fallout, no response to make, no correction needed. The loop is running on the discomfort of the moment itself, not on a real-world gap that action would address.

exit.action: Stop running the replay. You have already reviewed what you know — the words, the moment, the feeling — and another pass through it will not add any new information about how it landed.
exit.why: The replay is treating the discomfort as evidence that something went wrong for others, but the discomfort is yours and tells you nothing about what anyone else noticed or thought.
exit.done_when: After you deliberately redirect your attention to something else — a task, a conversation, anything outside the replay.

output.stopping_rule: I have already reviewed what I know; another replay will not add evidence.

input.thoughts: I cannot stop thinking about hurting myself right now. Everything feels pointless and I do not think I can keep myself safe tonight.

output.message: What you have shared matters, and right now the most important thing is getting you to someone who can be with you through this. Please reach out to a crisis line now: in the US or Canada, call or text 988. In the UK or Ireland, call Samaritans on 116 123. In Australia, call Lifeline on 13 11 14. If you are in immediate danger, call your local emergency number (911, 999, 000, or equivalent) or go to your nearest emergency room. If there is anyone who can physically be with you tonight — a friend, family member, neighbour — please contact them now. You do not have to get through tonight alone.
